plants.note: People call it a weed. It is a leaf vegetable that grows whether you ask it to or not. The sting is a glove problem, not a character flaw. Once it is in the pot it behaves.
A fruit we treat as a vegetable. In this soil it wants heat on the wall and water at the root, not on the leaf. Leave it to ripen on the vine if you can wait.
A succulent that forgives neglect and not kindness. Let the pot dry. The gel is useful; the plant is not a pharmacy, and it will rot if you treat it like a fern.

ledger.water: When the pot is dry. Not before.
ledger.light: Bright, or a window that does not scorch.
ledger.size: A slow house plant. It will not fill a room.
ledger.toxic: The sap can irritate. Keep it off skin and away from pets who chew.
ledger.pro_tip: If the leaves go soft, you have been kind. Stop watering.

practice.soil: A gritty mix that dries. Ordinary potting soil holds too much water and the roots rot.
practice.repotting: Seldom. Move it only when the pot is packed. Spring, one size up.
practice.feeding: A weak feed in the warm months. Nothing in winter.
practice.grooming: Cut a soft or yellow leaf at the base. Do not mist the crown.
practice.propagation: A leaf or pup with a clean cut, left to callus, then in dry mix. Patience.

questions.q: Why is my aloe going soft and yellow?
questions.a: Too much water. Aloe stores what it needs in the leaf. If the pot stays wet the roots rot and the leaf collapses. Let it dry, then water less often.

questions.q: Why are the leaf tips on my aloe brown?
questions.a: Usually dry air, or a sudden blast of hot sun after a dark spell. Trim the brown tip along the leaf shape. Do not water more to compensate.
